svg.aria-label: How each ND-500 addressing mode forms its effective address, one drawing per mode
svg.text: How the effective address is formed
B = base register, R = record register, Rn = index register R1..R4, d = displacement (unsigned), a = address, p = bytes per element of the data type.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: Post-index scale p, bytes per element

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: BI 1/8 BY 1 H 2 W 4 F 4 D 8 descriptor 8
Rn holds an element number, not a byte offset; the hardware multiplies by p. The next element is Rn + 1, whatever the type.
LOCAL, RECORD and CONSTANT each have a one-byte short form where the 6-bit field is the data itself.
For LOCAL and RECORD the short displacement counts words (ea = reg + d·4), so it reaches 0..63 words. The assembler picks the shortest form that fits.
Source: ND-05.009.4 ND-500 Reference Manual, chapter 8 (pages 97–101).
